text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- 1,500 Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) office and ground staff at Copenhagen airport are threatening to go on strike at Easter disrupting flights to and from Copenhagen International Airport if they cannot reach a new wage agreement before February 20.

--- Spanish contractor Sainco signed a 65 million crown contract with the Oeresund Consortium building a bridge-tunnel link between Sweden and Denmark to provide coast to coast technical installations.

--- Rail journeys between east and west Denmark will be one hour shorter from June when the Great Belt fixed link's tunnel and bridge open for passenger trains. Great Belt and Danish Rail(DSB) are currently training locomotive drivers to drive trains through the eight km undersea tunnel at speeds of 180 kph, a journey taking under ten minutes.
--- British actress Emily Watson has been nominated for a best actress Oscar for her role in Danish film director Lars Von Trier's "Breaking the Waves" movie.

--- Danish interest rates are at their lowest levels in two years and finance minister Mogens Lykketoft expects the fall to continue, sparking increased business investment and creating more jobs. Lykketoft also expects the Danish-German yield gap to narrow from its present 65 points.

--- Denmark's electricity industry is suffering from a lack of competition and Danish electricity prices are kept artificially low by indirect public subsidies to the tune of six billion crowns annually, a new report shows.
